notes:
Opportunity summary: Northhaven is a payments orchestration platform with latency-sensitive real-time decisioning + customer support routing. They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a mix of production traffic (primary) and training-like batch reranking (secondary).

Core requirements / constraints (extracted from calls):
- Hard SLOs: p50 <= 80ms for short-turn chat/decisioning (<=64 tokens), p95 <= 250ms for 512-token generation, p99 target 500-700ms. Must have SLO-backed credit/penalty language in SLA.
- Throughput target: sustained 30k inference requests/day with burst concurrency up to 1.2k rps for short requests during peak windows.
- Reserved GPU planning ask: initial commit plan is 8 x 80GB-class GPUs for critical path (estimate), ability to burst to additional 8 GPUs in dedicated cluster for seasonal peaks. Budget sensitivity — prefer predictable reserved capacity vs high variable spend.
- Autoscaling needs: prefer fast scale-up (<90s) and graceful scale-down (>10m cool-down) to avoid oscillation; warm pool of 2-3 pre-warmed GPUs per zone to absorb sudden bursts. Must minimize cold-start latency for KV-heavy models (cold-start observed ~40-60s with current runtime).
- Batching & queueing: want deterministic maximum queue depth (backpressure) to preserve p95; asked for options to set hard request queue cap per model and route overflow to cheaper fallback model.
- Fallbacks & routing: require automatic fallback to a 2x quantized model variant with consistent output semantics for up to 20% of traffic when capacity constrained. Prefer policy-based routing by latency SLO, cost tier, and region.
- Observability: token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 histograms, per-route concurrency, queue-length time series; request sampling that includes input+kvcache keys for troubleshooting.
- Security: KMS integration non-negotiable, audit logs 12+ months, SSO SAML, SOC2 Type II. Customer wants commitment to not persist PII in logs.

POC highlights (from 2024-12 POC):
- Test model: mid-size encoder-decoder variant with KV cache. Baseline cluster: 8x A100 80GB.
- Observed steady-state: 800 rps (short tokens) with p95 ~210ms when batching enabled (dynamic batching, 16-32 token batches).
- Burst test (simulate 1.2k rps): with 2 pre-warmed GPUs we saw queue growth and p95 spiked to 480ms on some runs; warm pool of 3 reduced spike frequency but did not eliminate p99 outliers.
- Cold-start measurement: new node spin+warm took 45-70s depending on model variant and KV cache restore; suggestion: keep a minimal hot pool and faster image startup to meet <90s scale-up target.
- Queueing behavior: default queue length allowed unbounded growth in POC; recommended implement hard caps + overflow routing to fallback model and early rejection with descriptive error to caller.

Recommended Redwood config to propose (draft):
- Reserved: 8 GPUs committed (primary), burst pool size policy to add up to +8 GPUs within 3 minutes (pre-warm strategy), warm pool = 3 GPUs per AZ.
- Autoscale: multi-signal autoscaler (rps, avg-latency, queue-depth) with scale-up aggressive (threshold breach 2 consecutive 15s windows) and scale-down conservative (cooldown 10m).
- Warm pools: maintain small hot pool with preloaded KV caches for top-3 models; lazy-loading for long-tail models. Warm pool replenishment policy: replace evicted warm node within 60s.
- Queue & backpressure: hard queue cap per model (configurable), overflow to quantized fallback model, expose queue-length metric and token-drop event.
- SLA ask (customer): 99.9% uptime for dedicated cluster, p95 latency credit for missed SLOs, ability to escalate for region outage. Redwood commercial to propose explicit SLO credits and trial SLA term.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Procurement prefers a 12mo reserved contract with monthly true-ups. Looking for blended rate that includes warm-pool reservation.
- Legal asked for indemnity carve-outs around 3rd-party model failures; Redwood to confirm standard terms.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Exact GPU family preference (customer leaning to H100 for future headroom, but A100 accepted for pricing). Need to show perf delta (p95) and OPEX impact.
- Confirm acceptable cold-start window (they requested <90s) and provide runbook for warm pool replenishment.
- Legal to receive clean SLA draft and proposed credit schedule by 2025-01-22.

Sales tactics / notes:
- Emphasize Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce reserved sizing by 20–30% via KV caching and batching.
- Offer 60-day pilot with committed warm pool and data residency paperwork completed as gating deliverable.
- Quote: draft committed proposal attached (drive:Northhaven-RI-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf).

Short quoted lines from stakeholders: "We need predictable latency during payment windows — variability is our biggest risk" — VP Product.
"If the warm pool costs too much, procurement will push back; need strong TCO model" — Head of Infra.

Next steps (short):

- Maeve to circulate SLA draft and commercial term sheet 2025-01-15.
- Legal & Procurement review meetings scheduled for week of 2025-01-20.
